His early works weredark, thickly painted, and sometimes wildly erotic. Butunder Pissarro's influence, his paletteand his touchlightenedandhe tued to the study of nature. Despite contact with the Impressionists, Cezanne's abrasive intensity and social awkwardness made him the outsider of the group. And where the Impressionists were concerned with surface appearance Cezanne was preoccupied with structure, and with how torepresent the solid, three-dimensional features of nature on the flat surface of a canvas.

Working painstakingly slowly， pnting tem motifs overand overagain, Cezanne developed an entirely original pictorial language in which depth and solidity arecreated notthrough conventional perspective andmodelling, butby subtly varying colours, and by distorting and tilting forms. Cézanne'swork hada profound influence on 20th-century artists, paving theway for Cubism and abstractart.
